title: Kevin Phillips Publishes 'The Emerging Republican Majority' Codifying Racial Realignment Strategy
summary: Kevin Phillips, a 28-year-old Nixon campaign strategist, published 'The Emerging Republican Majority,' which became the definitive blueprint for the Republican Party's Southern Strategy. The nearly 500-page book, with 47 maps and 143 charts, explicitly argued that 'the Negro problem, having become a national rather than a local one, is the principal cause of the breakup of the New Deal coalition.' Phillips was remarkably candid that racial resentment would drive a Republican realignment: 'For Phillips, it was almost inevitable that most whites would abandon the Democratic Party once it became identified with blacks.' The book argued that Republicans could build a durable majority by appealing to white voters in the South and 'Sun Belt'—a term the book coined—who opposed civil rights advances. Newsweek labeled it 'the political bible of the Nixon Era.' Phillips's predictions proved accurate for presidential elections over the next quarter century. The book represents a critical moment when racial dog whistle politics transitioned from implicit campaign tactics to explicit party strategy documented in writing. Phillips later became a critic of the Republican Party, but his 1969 work provided the intellectual framework for decades of coded racial appeals that would reshape American politics.
